Result: Editor launches normally. 


Forcing Vulkan does allow the editor to launch, and I'm assuming would allow games compiled to run.

As a note, my understanding of Windows on ARM is that it uses a software OpenGL compatibility stack to provide it on Adreno GPUs. 

I believe more details that may be helpful can be found here:

https://devblogs.microsoft.com/directx/announcing-the-opencl-and-opengl-compatibility-pack-for-windows-10-on-arm/

> OpenGL API 4.2 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.2.0-devel (git-18ad21fdfc) - Compatibility

and in  `4.5-dev3`?  _(`Mesa` looks suspicious)_

Further testing would make it seem likely an update either on Microsoft's or Lenovo's side has introduced this issue, as previously working builds are no longer starting either. 

Apologies for the random ping, @JustinBeckerMSFT I know that you are usually interested in issues matching this description and may be able to assist more directly. If you become available to have a look and are interested in doing so, the current non-beta native build of the Godot editor appears to be crashing on the X13s in the default DirectX 12 rendering mode, along with all dev builds.
@ggppjj thanks for the ping! I was able to repro the issue on my end, and it appears to be a bug with the OpenGlOn12 layer. I will report this to the owning team on our side.

## Confirmed: Same crash occurs across multiple Godot versions on ARM64

**Device:** Surface Pro 9 with Microsoft SQ3 @ 3.00 GHz  
**OS:** Windows 11 ARM64 (24H2)  
**Affected versions:** 4.4.1-stable, 4.5-dev5 (likely affects all recent ARM64 builds)

### Crash Details:
- **Module:** OpenGLOn12.dll (version 0.0.0.0)
- **Exception Code:** 0xc0000005 (Access Violation)
- **Behavior:** Godot launches, loads editor settings, then crashes silently during UI rendering phase

### Event Viewer Log:
```
Faulting application name: Godot_v4.5-dev5_windows_arm64.exe, version: 4.5.0.0
Faulting module name: OpenGLOn12.dll, version: 0.0.0.0
Exception code: 0xc0000005
```

### Console output before crash:
```
EditorTheme: Generating new styles.
EditorSettings: Save OK!
[Process terminates silently]
```

### **Workarounds that work:**

**Option 1 - Mobile Rendering (RECOMMENDED for stability):**
```bash
Godot_v4.x-xxx_windows_arm64.exe --rendering-method mobile --verbose
```

**Option 2 - Vulkan (works for editor, but unstable for projects):**
```bash
Godot_v4.x-xxx_windows_arm64.exe --rendering-driver vulkan --verbose
```

### Root Cause Analysis:
This appears to be a **systematic compatibility issue between Godot's OpenGL implementation and Microsoft's OpenGLOn12.dll translation layer** on Windows ARM64. The issue affects:

1. **All recent Godot ARM64 builds** (4.4.1, 4.5-dev5, possibly others)
2. **Surface devices with Qualcomm Adreno GPUs** (SQ2, SQ3, Snapdragon X series)
3. **Recent Windows 11 ARM64 builds** (especially after March 2025 updates)

**Multiple rendering paths affected differently:**
- **OpenGL3 + force-gl-es3**: Still crashes with OpenGLOn12.dll (0xc0000005)
- **OpenGL3 (default)**: Crashes silently with OpenGLOn12.dll
- **Vulkan**: Works for editor but has severe memory management issues causing crashes during intensive use
- **Mobile rendering**: Works stably by avoiding problematic OpenGL features

### Why different workarounds work:
- **Vulkan**: Bypasses OpenGLOn12 translation layer entirely, but Mesa Vulkan drivers have memory leaks
- **Mobile rendering**: Uses simplified OpenGL calls that don't trigger OpenGLOn12 bugs

### Suggested Solutions:

**Short-term:**
1. **Document Mobile rendering workaround** in ARM64 installation instructions as primary solution
2. Document Vulkan workaround with memory usage warnings
3. Consider making Mobile rendering the **default for ARM64 builds**
4. Add automatic fallback to Mobile rendering when OpenGLOn12 crash is detected

**Long-term:**
1. Investigate compatibility with newer OpenGLOn12.dll versions
2. Improve Vulkan memory management on Mesa drivers
3. Consider shipping ARM64 builds with Mobile rendering as default
4. Add better error handling/reporting when OpenGLOn12 fails

### Additional Context:
This issue seems related to **recent Windows 11 ARM64 updates** (KB5053598 and later) that modified the OpenGL compatibility layer. Multiple ARM64 applications experienced similar crashes around March 2025:

* [Windows 11 KB5053598 March update causing widespread crashes](https://www.windowslatest.com/2025/03/13/windows-11-kb5053598-issues-install-fails-rdp-disconnects-bsods-windows-11-24h2/)
* [Microsoft Community reports of display/color issues after KB5053598](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2225089/2025-03-cumulative-update-for-windows-11-version-2)
* [Java applications hanging after KB5053598 on ARM64](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/discussions/windows11/2025-03-cumulative-update-for-windows-11-version-24h2-for-arm64-based-systems-kb/4393427)

The crash occurs specifically during **editor UI initialization**, suggesting the issue is with OpenGL calls made during theme/style generation rather than core engine functionality.

**Impact:** This effectively makes Godot unusable out-of-the-box on ARM64 devices unless users know to use the Mobile rendering or Vulkan workarounds.

### **CONFIRMED: Blender 4.2.0 also affected with same OpenGLOn12.dll crash**

Testing revealed this is **not a Godot-specific issue** but a **systematic Windows ARM64 OpenGL problem**:

**Blender 4.2.0 crash details:**
```
ExceptionCode    : EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION  
Exception Module : OpenGLOn12.dll
Exception Address: 0x00007FFE14E02D24
Stack trace: OpenGLOn12.dll → mesa_glapi_get_proc_address → blender.exe → GPU_texture_update_sub → UI_block_draw
```

**Software rendering attempt shows underlying issue:**
```bash
# With LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
Warning! Using result of ChoosePixelFormat.
Implementation unexpectedly missing WGL_ARB_extensions_string. Probably a libepoxy bug.
```

**Root cause analysis:**
- **libepoxy library** (used by both Godot and Blender) cannot find WGL_ARB_extensions_string
- **OpenGLOn12.dll** doesn't properly implement OpenGL extension discovery on ARM64
- **Multiple professional applications affected**: Godot, Blender, likely others using OpenGL

### Additional Testing Results:

**Commands tested on Surface Pro 9 (SQ3):**
- `--rendering-driver opengl3 --force-gl-es3` → Crash (0xc0000005)
- `--rendering-driver vulkan` → Works for editor, memory crashes in projects  
- `--rendering-method mobile` → **Stable for both editor and projects**
- `--rendering-driver gles3` → Invalid driver error (not available in 4.x)

**Event Viewer consistently shows:**
```
Faulting module name: OpenGLOn12.dll
Exception code: 0xc0000005
```

**Vulkan memory errors include:**
```
VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY
VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY  
VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST
D3D12 device removed (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
```

Issue created on OpenCLOn12 Microsoft repo: https://github.com/microsoft/OpenCLOn12/issues/68

I didnt have success with `--rendering-method mobile`, it seemed like it was still starting vulkan.

Reverting to an older release of OpenCLOn12 fixes the startup issue, no flags neede. (Temporary fix until MS fix)

ex. https://github.com/microsoft/OpenCLOn12/releases/tag/v1.2404.1.0

Reverted from version : 1.2506.2.0

> --rendering-driver opengl3 --force-gl-es3 

This is not a valid argument, currently GLES on Windows is only supported with Angle, try `--rendering-driver opengl3_angle`. If binary was compiled with static Angle (official builds are), it will use it, if not it will try to load EGL dll, so it can be used with system EGL/GLES (or any other implementation) if no Angle dlls are in the same folder as executable.

> I didnt have success with --rendering-method mobile, it seemed like it was still starting vulkan

This is expected, there are two arguments `rendering-method` and `rendering-driver`. For `mobile` and `forward_plus` methods, driver can be either `vulkan` or `d3d12` (or `metal` on macOS/iOS), for `compatibility` methods, driver is variant of OpenGL.

## Update: Found the root cause and fix

Hi! I did some deep investigation after my previous comment and found the actual problem and a working solution.

The issue is in Microsoft's OpenCL/OpenGL Compatibility Pack (Microsoft.D3DMappingLayers), not in Godot. The current Store version (v1.2510.1.0) has a bug in OpenGLOn12.dll that causes crashes in multiple applications including Godot and Blender on Windows ARM64.

**Working fix:**

Downgrade to v1.2403.9.0 from GitHub:

1. Uninstall current version:
```powershell
Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.D3DMappingLayers | Remove-AppxPackage
```

2. Download v1.2403.9.0:
https://github.com/microsoft/OpenCLOn12/releases/download/v1.2403.9.0/Universal_D3DMappingLayers_1.2403.9.0_arm64.appx

3. Install it:
```powershell
Add-AppxPackage -Path "Universal_D3DMappingLayers_1.2403.9.0_arm64.appx"
```

4. Block automatic updates (recommended):
```powershell
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsStore" /v AutoDownload /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsStore\WindowsUpdate" /v AutoDownload /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
```
Even with these, Windows might still update it. If that happens, just reinstall v1.2403.9.0 again. Keep the appx file as a backup. Also avoid opening Microsoft Store or running winget upgrade --all.

5. Verify the version:
```powershell
Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.D3DMappingLayers | Select-Object Version
```
Should show: 1.2403.9.0

After this, Godot works perfectly with OpenGL renderer, no need for the Vulkan workaround.

I've documented the full investigation in the Microsoft OpenCLOn12 issue:
https://github.com/microsoft/OpenCLOn12/issues/68

This confirms it's a third-party bug in Microsoft's compatibility layer, not a Godot regression.

**Credit where due:** Just noticed @luciantin mentioned the downgrade solution back in June. I completely missed that. In retrospect, Windows probably auto-updated the package silently on my system after I tried it, which made the crash come back and I thought it didn't work.
